import pandas as pd

# Paths to source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_14/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_14/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_14/training_2.csv"

# Read source CSVs with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)

# UNION operation: concatenate all source dataframes
df_union = pd.concat([df0, df1, df2], ignore_index=True)

# Ensure columns are in the target schema order and types:
# Target Schema: ['username': float, 'date': string, 'retweets': integer, 'favorites': integer,
# 'text': string, 'geo': string, 'mentions': string, 'hashtags': string, 'id': float, 'permalink': string]

# Convert columns to target types:

# username: float (currently NaN in examples, so convert to float)
df_union['username'] = pd.to_numeric(df_union['username'], errors='coerce')

# date: string (ensure string type)
df_union['date'] = df_union['date'].astype(str)

# retweets: integer
df_union['retweets'] = pd.to_numeric(df_union['retweets'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# favorites: integer
df_union['favorites'] = pd.to_numeric(df_union['favorites'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# text: string
df_union['text'] = df_union['text'].astype(str)

# geo: string, keep NaN as is (will be saved as empty string or NaN)
df_union['geo'] = df_union['geo'].astype(str).replace('nan', pd.NA)

# mentions: string, keep NaN as is
df_union['mentions'] = df_union['mentions'].astype(str).replace('nan', pd.NA)

# hashtags: string, keep NaN as is
df_union['hashtags'] = df_union['hashtags'].astype(str).replace('nan', pd.NA)

# id: float
df_union['id'] = pd.to_numeric(df_union['id'], errors='coerce')

# permalink: string
df_union['permalink'] = df_union['permalink'].astype(str)

# Reorder columns exactly as target schema
target_columns = ['username', 'date', 'retweets', 'favorites', 'text', 'geo', 'mentions', 'hashtags', 'id', 'permalink']
df_target = df_union[target_columns]

# Write the final dataframe to the target CSV path without the index
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_14/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_14/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_14/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_14/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join source1 and source2 to source0 on 'id' column (inner join to keep only matching ids)
df_join_01 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on='id', how='inner', suffixes=('_0', '_1'))
df_join_all = pd.merge(df_join_01, source2, on='id', how='inner', suffixes=('', '_2'))

# After join, columns from source0, source1, source2 exist with suffixes
# We want to produce a single table with columns as in target schema:
# ['username', 'date', 'retweets', 'favorites', 'text', 'geo', 'mentions', 'hashtags', 'id', 'permalink']

# For each column except 'id', take the max (non-null) value across the three sources
# Because all sources have same schema, columns from source0 have no suffix,
# source1 columns have suffix '_1', source2 columns have suffix '_2'

# Define columns to aggregate (all except 'id')
cols = ['username', 'date', 'retweets', 'favorites', 'text', 'geo', 'mentions', 'hashtags', 'permalink']

# Create a DataFrame to hold aggregated results
agg_dict = {}
for col in cols:
    # Columns from each source after join
    col_0 = col + '_0' if col != 'id' else 'id'  # source0 columns have suffix '_0' after first merge
    col_1 = col + '_1'
    col_2 = col + '_2'
    # For 'id', only one column exists (no suffix)
    if col == 'id':
        agg_dict[col] = 'first'
    else:
        # max to pick non-null string or numeric value (max works for strings lex order)
        agg_dict[col] = lambda x: x.dropna().max() if not x.dropna().empty else pd.NA

# Group by 'id' and aggregate
# But after join, 'id' is unique key, so groupby is trivial, just aggregate per row
# So we can apply aggregation row-wise

def aggregate_row(row):
    res = {}
    for col in cols:
        if col == 'id':
            res[col] = row['id']
        else:
            vals = []
            for suffix in ['_0', '_1', '_2']:
                col_name = col + suffix
                if col_name in row and pd.notna(row[col_name]):
                    vals.append(row[col_name])
            if vals:
                # For numeric columns, max is fine
                # For string columns, max picks lex max, which is acceptable to pick one non-null value
                res[col] = max(vals)
            else:
                res[col] = pd.NA
    return pd.Series(res)

df_aggregated = df_join_all.apply(aggregate_row, axis=1)

# Ensure columns order as target schema
df_aggregated = df_aggregated[['username', 'date', 'retweets', 'favorites', 'text', 'geo', 'mentions', 'hashtags', 'id', 'permalink']]

# Write to output CSV
df_aggregated.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_14/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
